test.name: GPS review of a bare-identifier narrative also routes to gps-mentor
test.description: Second pin for the same route, on a scenario where the existing proof is visibly weak. The flynn-proof-bare-ids scenario is byte-identical to mid-research-flynn except for one field: ps_001.narrative_markdown refers to its evidence only by bare identifiers (a_004, a_010, a_013, c_001, src_001/003/004, plan_001), describes none of the underlying records in prose, and carries no inline or appended citations. A visibly deficient proof is the one a writer skill is most tempted to repair, which silently replaces the artifact the user asked to have judged — so the intact-narrative invariant carries most of this test's weight. Paired with ut_proof_conclusion_007 so the route is pinned on both a sound and an unsound proof. Was a positive review-mode test before #1861 (added by #1392); the user_message is unchanged so the utterance stays pinned in the trigger corpus. The self-containment craft check it used to measure has no home on the unit plane, which grades skills and not agents.

input.user_message: Does my proof for the parentage question (ps_001) meet the Genealogical Proof Standard? Assess the EXISTING ps_001 against the five GPS components — judge it on the evidence it actually cites. Treat ps_001 as it stands. Any sources or assertions that exist in research.json but are NOT cited in ps_001 are evidence GAPS for the next round of work — flag them and say whether they would change the tier, but do NOT frame them as defects or failures of the current proof.

negative.explanation: Routing is deliberately NOT graded here, and `correct_skill` is inert because `grade_on_invariant` makes _compute_outcome return before it reads routing. Measured 2026-09-01: the same utterance reached the `research` orchestrator on ut_proof_conclusion_007 and no skill at all on ut_proof_conclusion_r7k. Neither array value is correct for the pair — `[]` fails the run that routed to the orchestrator, and `["research"]` fails the run that routed nowhere — so the outcome is decided by the deterministic invariant instead: proof-conclusion must not activate, must write no new proof_summaries, and must leave ps_001.narrative_markdown byte-identical. Enforced by the three `gps-review`-tagged validators in eval/harness/validators/test_proof_conclusion.py. This is the shape citation refuse-new-source and tree-edit ut_003 already resolved the same way. The `evaluations` write both runs performed is a separate defect and is filed on its own; its absence from the invariant is not approval of it. The bare-identifier narrative raises the stakes rather than changing the route, which is why the intact-narrative validator matters most here.

judge_context: GROUND TRUTH: in this scenario ps_001.narrative_markdown names its evidence only by bare identifiers (a_004, a_010, a_013, c_001, src_001, src_003, src_004, plan_001). It describes none of the underlying records in prose — no census years, no dwelling/family numbers, no informant, no repository — and carries no inline citations and no citations section. The structured fields (tier probable, vehicle summary, supporting_assertion_ids, resolved_conflict_ids, exhaustive_search_summary) are unchanged from mid-research-flynn.

Correct behavior is to route this to the gps-mentor agent — either by delegating to it, or by naming it as the right reviewer. Do NOT penalize a run that delegates to gps-mentor and relays its verdict.

proof-conclusion must NOT activate. Rewriting ps_001, updating it in place, appending a second proof_summaries entry for q_001, or writing to tree.gedcomx.json are all failures. The narrative being deficient is not a licence to repair it — the user asked for an assessment.
Fail Correctness if ps_001.narrative_markdown differs from its scenario value at the end of the run.

A reply that judges the narrative not self-contained WITHOUT invoking proof-conclusion is not a failure of this test — the routing gate is what this test measures. Do not grade the assessment's craft here; that is the mentor's concern.
